reason: E2 and E3 directly show that Mn addition introduces magnetic frustration and breaks the trend for relative fcc/hcp energies, while CrCoNi exhibits an hcp ground state and deformation-induced hcp nanostructure. E1 confirms CrCoNi's superior properties but does not itself link them to the transformation, leaving a minor gap in directly evidencing the causal link between transformation and mechanical enhancement.
premises: Mn in CrMnFeCoNi causes magnetic frustration that inhibits fcc-to-hcp transformation
Mn-reduced alloys (e.g., CrCoNi) undergo deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation at defects
The fcc-to-hcp transformation is driven by favorable magnetic interactions among Cr, Co, Ni
The transformation enhances strain hardening and delays failure
The quinary alloy lacks this transformation-based strengthening due to Mn-induced frustration
